draft.title: Modelling with functions
card: Linear
y = mx + c. The value changes by the same amount each step. m is the rate of change and c is the starting value.
Quadratic
y = ax² + bx + c. The graph has one turning point, so it suits a rise then a fall, such as a ball thrown in the air.
Exponential
y = A × bˣ. The value is multiplied by the same factor each step. A is the starting value. If b > 1 it grows, and if 0 < b < 1 it decays.
Trigonometric
y = k sin(a(x + b)) + c repeats in a cycle, so it suits tides. c is the average level, k is the amplitude and 2π/a is the period.
draft.remember: Same amount added: linear. Same factor multiplied: exponential. Repeating cycle: trigonometric.

a.q: A town has 2000 people. Its population grows by 5% each year. Which model suits this best?
a.why: A 5% rise each year means multiplying by the same factor, 1.05, every year. That is exponential. A linear model adds the same number of people each year, which is not what a percentage rise does.
a.clue: Is the same amount added, or the same factor multiplied?

b.q: The depth of water in a harbour is D = 6 + 2 sin(πt/6) metres, where t is hours. What is the depth when the water is at its highest?
b.why: The centre line is 6 and the amplitude is 2, so the highest depth is 6 + 2 = 8 metres. The tempting answer is 2 metres, but that is only the amplitude, which is the distance above the centre line, not the depth.
b.clue: Add the amplitude to the centre line.

problems.detail: The trigonometric line explains that k is the amplitude, 2π/a the period and c the centre line. That is the content of point 2 (Transforming trigonometric graphs), which is taught here rather than only mentioned. Question b then relies on it.
The letter b means the growth factor in y = A × bˣ but the phase shift in y = k sin(a(x + b)) + c. Using the same letter for two different things on one card could confuse students.

check.summary: Both questions are correct and have one clear answer. The card re-teaches the trigonometric parameters (amplitude, period, centre line) that belong to point 2, and it uses b for two different meanings.

proposal.title: Modelling with functions
card: Linear
y = mx + c. The value changes by the same amount each step. m is the rate of change and c is the starting value.
Quadratic
y = ax² + bx + c. The graph has one turning point, so it suits a rise then a fall, such as a ball thrown in the air.
Exponential
y = A × rˣ: A is the starting value and each step multiplies by r, so r > 1 grows and 0 < r < 1 decays. In P = 300 × 0.9ᵗ, each step keeps 90%, so 10% is lost.
Trigonometric
A sine or cosine model repeats the same cycle over and over, so it suits things that rise and fall regularly, such as tides or daylight hours.
proposal.remember: Same amount added: linear. Same factor multiplied: exponential. One turning point: quadratic. Repeating cycle: trigonometric.

a.q: A town has 2000 people. Its population grows by 5% each year. Which model suits this best?
a.why: A 5% rise each year means multiplying by the same factor, 1.05, every year. That is exponential. A linear model adds the same number of people each year, which is not what a percentage rise does.
a.clue: Is the same amount added, or the same factor multiplied?

b.q: A car's value is V = 30000 × 0.85ᵗ dollars, where t is years. What does 0.85 tell you?
opts: It loses 15% of its value each year
It loses 85% of its value each year
It loses $0.85 of its value each year
It keeps 15% of its value each year
b.why: Multiplying by 0.85 means the car keeps 85% of its value each year, so it loses 100% − 85% = 15%. Losing 85% each year would need a factor of 0.15, not 0.85.
b.clue: Multiplying by 0.85 keeps what share of the value?

b.best: It loses 15% of its value each year
